title: Single, multiple and extending beds
intro: Compare a single bed, two separate beds and pull-out or extending systems through access, support and transformation states. A compact closed footprint is not sufficient to approve a mechanism.
goals: Compare sleeping places and use patterns
Draw closed, transition and occupied states
Verify mechanism, support and mattress compatibility

sections.title: Compare sleeping places and use patterns
sections.text: Define users, sleeping frequency and independent entry/exit. Two separate beds have different envelopes and routes from a single bed or a pull-out lower bed. Check whether the deployed bed blocks a door or drawer. Elevated beds require the separate safety review in the next lesson; lack of floor space does not by itself justify elevating a sleeping place.
sections.caption: Compare occupied sleeping states, not only closed footprints.

sections.title: Draw closed, transition and occupied states
sections.text: Draw components before, during and after movement, identifying hand/body paths, pinch/shear locations and the deployed supports. Do not use a child to trial an unverified mechanism. Have the specified system’s motion, protection and retention reviewed competently first; assess appropriate use only after acceptance and in accordance with the product instructions.
sections.caption: Transition states need review as well as the final position.

sections.title: Verify mechanism, support and mattress compatibility
sections.text: Identify the system, compatible mattress, use limits, required retention/stops, floor conditions and maintenance instructions. A large drawer does not become a bed merely because it pulls out, and wheels do not establish sleeping-load support or stability. Refer changes to length, support or mechanism to the manufacturer or competent reviewer before implementation.
sections.caption: Verify a sleeping system rather than relabeling a drawer.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The pull-out option frees daytime space but blocks the entrance route when occupied. Revise the arrangement or compare separate beds against the programme. Do not approve it solely because the closed-state illustration looks more spacious.
example.decision: Decision: review sleeping, transition and access states before selection.

quiz.question: Which state must be included when comparing a pull-out bed?
options: Deployed occupied state and access route
quiz.explanation: The occupied footprint can obstruct access even when the closed state is compact.

assignment.prompt: Compare the bed options and draw closed/transition/deployed states with required compatibility information.

faq.question: Can any wheeled drawer serve as a bed?
faq.answer: No. It must be a verified sleeping system with appropriate support, mattress compatibility and stability.
